entries.german: XII b. Graf Boppo von Werlheim verleiht, vor seinem Zuge zum h. Grabe, der Cistercienser Abtei Alten berg (am Niederrhein) Zollfreiheit in seiner Graf schaft 1183. C. In nomine sanete et indiuidue trinitatis. Boppo dei gratia Comes de Wertheym. Pax, uictoria regnumque per nenne Christi et ecclesie feliciter in euum permaneat. Quoniam ea que in mundo sunt agili fluxu et celeri cursu cuneta pretereunt et ea que non sunt superueniunt, mirandum non est, si mortalium queque facta quasi cum ipsis morientia recedunt et quasi non fuerint sie uniuersa erunt. Proinde uero est quod rationi bene congruit, scilicet quod sacra priuilegiorum sanetione quelibet pia nobilium ac poten- tum gesta in posterum muniantur. Ut igitur hec presens do natio uniuersis fidelibus Christo et ecclesie deuotis semper pateat, hec mea testimentalis tuba in omni personet euo. Quoniam ego Boppo dei gratia Comes de Wertheym nobilitate prepollens diuiciis deliciisque alfluens grauibus delictis et noxialibus peccatis dominum deum grauiter offendisse intra me extimui, meque ad placandum ipsum regem celorum ultra maris alueum Ihrosolimam iturum deuotaui, ibique sanctissimum sepulchrum domini christianissima fide uisitaturum optaui, summopere sperans meque consolans per regem et sacerdo- tem uerum Samaritanum nostrum miseros errores meos abo- \\ertbeim. Hec itaque salutaria uota mecum reuoluens ad dilectum locum Bergen eis rhenum positum porrexi, ibique propter eterne uite premium mihi meisque caris uiuis ac defunetis promerendum domino Jesu Christo ejusque intemerate genilrici perpetue uirgini Marie eunetis- que fratribus ibidem deo deuotis omne theloneum ex tmiuer— sis bonis suis, nauigio transuehendis, quod in mei jurisdi- tione jure regio mihi adtrahere et in usus meos colligere de- bui perpetua stabilitatc seruitium delegans, donaui et hoc cum dileeta conjuge mea Cunegunda et cum unicis meis li~ beris coram testibus idoneis inviolabiliter stabiliui. Ad hujus uero donationis probabilem euidentiam firmissime constitui, quatinus uniuersi ex hoc cenobio equites et pedites sine na uigio castrum meum transeuntes in omnibus presidatus atque regiminis mei terminis absque omnimoda lesione et grauamine nostro et successorum nostrorum presidio semper securi et tuti ueniant et ad sua feliciter redeant, nobisque deuotas orationes suas in domino ipsi rependant. Hec itaque donatio nis pagina ut in suo debito uigore intacta et inlesa perma- neat, nostri sigilli impressio in omne euum perhenniter atque irreuocabiliter ipsam corroborat. entries.english:
XIIb. Count Boppo von Wertheim grants toll exemption throughout his county to the Cistercian Abbey of Altenberg on the Lower Rhine before his journey to the Holy Sepulchre. 1183.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Boppo, by the grace of God Count von Wertheim. May peace, victory, and the kingdom of Christ and the Church endure happily forever. Since everything in this world passes swiftly away, and what was not there before comes in its place, it is no wonder that the deeds of mortals pass away as if they died with them, and all things become as though they had never been. It is therefore right and reasonable that the sacred authority of privileges should secure for the future every pious deed of noble and powerful people. So that this present donation may always be known to all the faithful devoted to Christ and the Church, let this testament of mine resound for all time.

I, Boppo, by the grace of God Count von Wertheim, distinguished in nobility and abundantly supplied with wealth and comforts, considered that I had gravely offended the Lord God through serious transgressions and harmful sins. To appease Him, I vowed to travel overseas to Jerusalem, the King of Heaven, and wished to visit the Lord’s most holy sepulchre in the Christian faith, hoping and consoling myself greatly that through our true King and Priest, the Good Samaritan, my wretched errors would be erased and the wounds and sicknesses of my soul healed there completely.

As I reflected upon these salutary vows, I went to the beloved place of Bergen on the Rhine. There, for the sake of earning eternal life for myself and my dear ones, living and dead, I donated to the Lord Jesus Christ, His immaculate mother, the perpetual Virgin Mary, and all the brothers there devoted to God, in perpetual and stable service, all tolls on their goods transported by ship which, by royal right, I could exact within my jurisdiction and collect for my own use. I made and confirmed this grant irrevocably before suitable witnesses, together with my beloved wife Cunigunda and my only children.

As reliable proof of this donation, I firmly established that all members of this monastery, on horseback or on foot, crossing my castle without a ship, shall always travel safely and securely, without injury or burden from me or my successors, throughout all the territories under my authority and rule, and return home safely; in return they shall offer us their devout prayers in the Lord. To ensure that this donation remains intact and unimpaired in its proper force, the impression of our seal confirms it forever, perpetually and irrevocably.

Witnesses: the entire sacred convent of that monastery; Abbot Eberolf of Brombach; Conrad von Wichardesheim; Arnold, son of Trutmann; Gumbert, toll collector of that same Count Boppo; Friedrich; and many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1183, in the first indiction, while the most blessed Lord Lucius, by the grace of God Pope, presided over the apostolic see; the invincible and most glorious Lord Frederick, by the grace of God Roman Emperor, ruled in the twentieth year of his empire; Lord Philip, by the grace of God Archbishop of the Holy Church of Cologne, and Lord Gozwin, most reverend abbot, held office; and Lord Reinhard, reverend Bishop of the Church of Würzburg.

[Printed in Th. J. Lacomblet, *Urkundenbuch für die Geschichte des Niederrheins*, Düsseldorf, 1840, vol. 1, p. 345, no. 489.]
